note: Names the rules profile and the drawings of this project, so no project name sits in the Python files. Paths are relative to the repo root, except inputRoot, which is the folder of the real input files on this machine. schedules names the two past schedule workbooks that the level proof reads from the References folder under inputRoot. drawings holds one file name per role. baseplan has the plot faces and labels. masterplan is the current master plan drawing, the second source check reads it and config/second_source.json names its plot layers. previousMasterplan is the master plan it replaced, kept for reference and not read in the full run. villaBlocks is the drawing the villa block of each unit is read from. roadLayout is the road layout drawing, its road edges give the front of a row. xrefRoles maps the name of an xref file that is not on disk to the role of the drawing that stands in for it. skip lists the other drawings the full run does not read, each with its reason. referenceOnly lists the drawings kept for reference only, R06_0000 and R06_0001 saved on this machine, which no villa block reader may take, since the villa blocks come from villaBlocks, the Building Footprint (Bader, Q045, R300). The analysis block holds how the CAD analysis reads the drawings. Lengths are in metres. partyWallShare is the share of plot.long_side that a shared edge must reach to count as a party wall. endShare is how far from the centre of a row, as a share of plot.long_side, a shared edge must lie to count as the front or the back of the row. roadEdgeLayers names the layers of the road layout drawing that hold the road edge polylines. unitPlotTypes lists the client plot types of the baseplan labels that stand for a plot with a unit on it, so only those plots get an issue when no unit code is found for them (R69). It is a list of plot types and never maps a plot type to a unit code (R30). noRev6Match lists the cluster codes of the profile that are old client codes with no Rev 6 cluster, and every cluster written with one of them gets an issue (R75). blockClusters maps the name of a footprint block to the cluster code it hints at, a block that stands for 2 or 4 plots says those plots are one cluster and it never gives a unit code to a plot (R90). The unit code of a plot is its Excel unit and nothing else (R69). pairRule false keeps the mirror flags of the blocks out of the row split until the original and mirror convention is known (R70). pastJob names what python/plan_from_past.py reads to build plan.json from a past job (R81). schedule is one of schedules and sheet is its sheet. prototypes is the full path of a kept copy of the prototypes.json the Revit reader wrote on the past model, since a later reader run writes prototypes.json again. prototypeFolder is the folder of the KEO prototype files under inputRoot, the Revit 2021 files of the past job, kept as the source. upgradedPrototypeFolder is the folder of their Revit 2024 copies with the same file names (R109), the folder plan.json gives the placer. output is the full path of the plan file, outside the repo. parameters lists the shared parameters to write on each link, RRE_ZZ_SP_Prototype-FFL is never one of them. testHost names what the Revit test host of R103 runs on. model is the site model under inputRoot that each run copies to <name>_TEST-<code>.rvt next to it, by a file copy only, and order is the prototype codes in the order they are tested, one per run. imageStepMinutes is the most the image step of an image job may run (Bader, Q061, R302), Run-TestHost.ps1 writes it into the job. imageMarginMinutes is what the job may run on top of it for the open and the close of the model, several times what the NBH 03 file took, whose measures are in steps/investigations/round-addin.md (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN). The job total is the two together and the window limit 3 minutes more. sampleSeconds is how often Run-TestHost.ps1 samples the private memory, working set and responding of its Revit and the free memory of the machine (R310), every 5 s as the sampler of I28 did (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN). cimTimeoutSeconds is the limit of each of the two CIM calls of a sample, the free memory and the child list, so a WMI that hangs never holds the wait loop, 2 s against the 42 to 109 ms the calls took on this machine, and two calls at it fit in the 5 s of the checks (CHOSEN, Round ADDIN review). helperProcesses names the processes Revit started in the window of KG3, conhost left out since every console has one, any of which a later window may reuse as it did the LocalDB of Steel Connections in Phase 1. Those already running at the start of a window are listed with their private memory in run.json, since the child figures of that window never count them (R310). pastJob.baseplanPlots is plots.json of the CAD reader run on the baseplan, relative to the repo root, and its plot faces give each yard floor its plot (R111). floors names what the floor step of the placer places (R112 to R116). types gives the floor type names of each kind, generic, yard and ramp, and the plan builder, the placer and the check use only these. keyTypes gives an answer key of answerKeys the type names of a kind its model names otherwise, FFL for the Generic floors of the IME and IMF keys (Round ADDIN Phase 1, READ from their reads), and a key reads the kinds it does not name by types (R321). levels gives the level of each kind. plotParameter is the floor parameter that holds unit-plot, for example VD2-2441, on all three kinds. yardBelowFflM is how far the top of the yard sits below the FFL (Bader, 24 Oct). yardShareTie is the share difference under which two plots tie for one yard. yardMinShare is the least share the best face must hold, under it the yard goes to no plot and is listed (round 15b review). cadLinks holds what the links from CAD are measured with (R120 to R123). cutShareMin is the share of its Generic floor that the baseplan face of a plot must hold, a plot under it does not follow the baseplan cut and is listed apart in every comparison (R120). cutNeighbours lists the plots Bader added to the cut plots, the neighbours of the listed plots whose links or ramps follow the past cut of those plots, and they are listed apart with them (R120). caseParameters names the link parameters the CASE test of R132 compares the second letter with. floorWidthStepM is the step the plot width is rounded to when the Generic and yard outlines are grouped (R135). planOutput is the full path of the plan python/plan_from_cad.py writes, outside the repo next to the plan of the past job (R128). handCheck lists the folders a read job of R245 may open a test copy in, the prototype copies of the data book (round DATA-4). siteBuild holds round Z4 (R200 to R219): folder is the round folder outside the repo with snapshot, work, images and logs under it, template the Revit 2024 metric template a newSite job starts from, newFile the name of the new site file in work, null between to delete, minFreeGB the free memory floor before a window, windowProcesses the processes that count as an open window, snapshot the data book files read in this round, roadSurfaces the LandXML parameterGroup the group of the new shared parameters, steepUnits the units whose ramp is Ramps 2% and whose El @ Entry takes the steep slope, rampDepthM the Rev 6 ramp depth by unit, bandsMm the slack a judged link may lie past the key (R227 to R229), and placeSettleMinutes how long free memory may take to come back over minFreeGB before no more prototype code is placed (R231). placerCheck read, plot by parameter or by the instance Name, datum none or the survey elevation, and floorTypes when its floors are of other types than floors.types. majority holds the share a rule must reach on the past plots to be strong (Round 17) pastAll names what python/past_all.py writes per plot of a past key (R269): linkParameters the link parameters, floorParameters those of the Generic floor of a Native key, and entryParameter the one of them that holds El @ Entry majority holds the majority rule of Round 17 (R270 to R276): strongShare the share a rule must reach to be strong, levelHoldMm how near a level must be to hold, entryRampM how far an El @ Entry parameter may sit off its own ramp top, groups the keys of each generation, codeFrom whether a group is read by its Rev 9 code or its own unit, slopeBands, depthBands and heightBands the bands of the factors, rampTypeClass the slope class each ramp type names, groupSlopes the slope each group is tested with for El @ Entry, sideShare the share of the plot depth two faces must share to be side neighbours, wholeFaceShare the overlap a Generic floor needs to be the whole face, parameterTests the link parameters tested, overrideDecisions the decisions whose misses go to config/overrides/roshn-makkah.json, overrideDefaultSources the sources, jobs of groups, a build applies when it names none, parsons, so the native overrides stay in the list and never apply by default (R330). rotationHoldDeg is how near the front frame a link rotation holds, the rotation tolerance of R122, linkHoldMm how near the plotFrame fit a link origin holds, the 10 mm band R121 fits by, since the plan and the key write a point to the mm, cornerFrontRule the front rule of R226 a corner plot is held on apart (Q037) and siteReference the key of each group the coordinates of every other read of that group are held against, the reference keys of the groups held against each other apart (R331, R332), check the seeds and the sample of python/key_rules_check.py (R336), the first seed also splitting the yard outlines into fit and test halves (R334), outlineHoldMm how near the rule each ramp corner and the boundary of a yard lie to hold, the 10 mm of R137, pairKinds the kinds of the units in no cluster paired along their row (R333) and flatRampType the ramp type whose class the flat ramps are counted by (R334). levelPassMm is the pass limit of a level of a group a build by keyRules builds (R339): a level holds when it lies within half a millimetre of the key, so two levels R67 rounds to the mm round to the same mm and an FFL, written to the mm, is equal, the levels to the mm Bader asked for (Round ADDIN 3c, CHOSEN). levelBandsMm are the bands the share of each level decision is also given at, 1 mm and the 5 mm of levelHoldMm, which Round 17 held the levels by. levelNotMeasured says per level a build gives that no key holds why it is not measured, SSL. parameterLevels are the link parameters that hold a level, held against the levels of the key within levelHoldMm and listed as gaps, linkNameFacade the parameters that end the link Name after plot, code and steps, wallTypes the pattern of the wall type of each kind of wall, wallCentreCodes the location line codes of Revit that lie on the wall or core centre, the others on a face, and frontOpenShare the share of the front edge a plot whose walls cover no more of it leaves open (R335). kindLeaveOut may also name one parameter decision whole, as the SE keys leave out parameter RRE_ZZ_SP_RVT-Name, which an STR link holds as plot | code (R335). answerKeys lists the answer keys of Round ADDIN and how their Revit 2024 copies are made (R312): folder is the copy folder under inputRoot, manifest the JSON file in it that python/key_copies.py writes, format the Revit version every copy must have by its bytes, jobPrefix the letter that starts the code of the siteUpgrade job of a key, before the letter of its IM code. codePrefix is what every key code starts with, IM, and one capital follows it, the letter the job code takes. zonePattern is the shape of a zone, kinds the kinds of a key, TU for the site models and SE for the structural ones. codeInName is where the copy name and the file name of the source of a key hold its code, {code} standing for it, so a name swapped between two keys is refused. Each key holds its IM code, zone, kind TU or SE, the source under inputRoot its copy is made from and the copy name, the name of its model in Revit All Zones. The IMC copy is made from the Zone 02 ARC original, the IMC key, and not from the zone2 IMC of Revit All Zones, which is the master of the floor scenarios (Q065). prototypeNames gives the parts every KEO prototype file name is made of, prefix, then the discipline, then -, the prototype code, suffix and a number, .rvt, with ARC the discipline of the prototypes of the plan (R313). Run-TestHost.ps1 reads them and writes them into every job that names a prototype file, and the guard of the test host takes them from the job. prototypeSets names the other prototype files an upgrade job may save as Revit 2024 files besides the ARC prototypes of the plan (R313): STR, the 13 structural prototypes the SE models of IMA and IMB link, from their 2021 folder into a folder of their own in upgradedPrototypeFolder, so the ARC prototypes the placer takes by code stay alone (Q067). discipline is the part of the file names after KEO, STR, and codePrefix starts the job code of each, S and the prototype code. keyPlans holds how plan_from_past.py --key builds the plan of an answer key (R325): wallEdgeM is how near the middle of a wall must lie to an edge of a generic floor for the wall to go to that plot, 0.3 m, since the walls of the IMC key sit 0.099 m (median) to 0.100 m (90th percentile) off the edge of their generic floor (Round ADDIN 2b, CHOSEN). entryHeightM is the band in metres the floor top must stand over the El @ Entry parameter of its generic floor for the value to be used, 0.0 to 1.5 m, since on the 7 keys every generic floor stands 0.05 to 0.8 m over it but 21, IMC 10 and IMD 4 whose value is 0, IMF 6 whose value is the placeholder 150.0 and IMD 1217, which stand 14.8 m to 174 m off it (Round ADDIN 2b review, CHOSEN). majority.groups.parsons names the 7 answer keys of Round ADDIN by their code in lower case, imc being the IMC key read in Round 17 and again from its 2024 copy, so each row of past_all.csv takes its job as its source (R326). majority.kindLeaveOut names, per kind of answer key, the decisions its rows are left out of: SE, the structural models of IMA and IMB, hold no level, ramp or yard floor of their own and their Generic floors carry the SE levels, so their rows never count for the ramp slope, El @ Entry, ramp front and its fall, the height, the steps or the yard (Q066, Round ADDIN 2b review). pastAll.scheduleKeys gives each pastSource of plots.csv the answer key whose job made that schedule, past job plan the IMC schedule by plan_imc_past.json and schedule IMD the IMD schedule, so past_all.py --schedule-entry gives El @ Entry of a schedule only to the key of its own job (R326). placerCheck.dialects.parsons reads an answer key as R325 builds its plan: each plot by the face its generic floor stands on, the plot number parameter of a link naming its floor, and no datum, since the 7 keys hold their levels in shared elevation. entrySpots holds how python/entry_spots.py looks for the spot elevations at the plot entrance (R327): radiiM the distances from the entrance point, the middle of the higher long edge of the ramp (R94), 0.5 m for a spot at that point and 6.0 m for the corners of that edge, which lie 5.0 m from its middle at the median on the IMC key, and cornerM how near a spot must lie to a corner of the entrance edge, 0.05 m as the spot check of R47 (Round ADDIN 2b, CHOSEN), and bandsM how near a spot value must lie to El @ Entry, 1 mm, the rounding of two values written to the mm by R2, and 5 mm, as majority.levelHoldMm (Round ADDIN 2b review)

cadReads.note: R388. The folder of the CadReader reads the measure (python/majority.py) and the build (python/plan_from_book.py) read, relative to the repo: the read folder of each drawing of drawings, baseplan, roadLayout and villaBlocks, with its layers.json, so both read one set through the units check. A file a run names that is not the one named here is taken only as a copy of its bytes by SHA-256, such as the outputs the Round 17 snapshot copied alone. R348, Round ADDIN 4c: the reads of the CadReader of 4c, round4c, in place of those of Round 12, written at 03:04 on 2026-10-24 before 4ac1428 turned the outline of a flipped insert back to counter clockwise (R68): the footprint blocks.json held 2,081 mirrored outlines the other way round, every other file the build and the measure read equal by SHA-256.

tableUnits.note: R388. The units of the tables of a data book reader that records none in the data.json of its table folder, by reader. The C3DProbe tables of the full Civil 3D read, of Makkah Phase 1_Road Layout, Road Surface C3D, Rough Grading and MP-SK-01-03-006_R9.0, carry none, and the CadReader reads of the same four drawings give Meters in their layers.json. The CadReader stand-in records the units of its drawing itself. A table of a reader named here by no unit is refused.

dataBook.note: R348, R350. The settings of the reads of button 2 (docs/addin-design.md 3.2), moved here from python/c3d_probe.json in Round ADDIN 4c so the worker and the Python readers take one copy: the curb, ROW and setback layers of join, the two Rev 9 workbooks with the DLUS setback and sales sheets of rev9, the area key sheets of data5.areaKey and the sales sheet of locationPlan, the one the build, the measure and the corner rule read. python/c3d_run.load_config lays this block over dataBook of the probe settings and refuses a key both files hold. The workbook paths are relative to the work folder of the data book, the worker takes the files of the pane by their role, addin.workbookRoles. The location plan settings move with R351 in Phase 4d.

controlMark.note: R387, Q081. The mark of a control point the sheet prints is a curve of this shape, width and height in pt within tolerancePt and its point count, the only three such curves of the page, one within controlSearchPt of each E = text. The control point fit starts from the similarity of the three marks.

The neighbourhood schedules of the location plan fit, moved here from connect of python/c3d_probe.json so the worker and the Python readers take one copy: the schedule workbook of each neighbourhood in the References folder of inputRoot and the shift from its baseplan label to its official number (R28), and scheduleSheet, the sheet of the plot table in each. dataBook.locationPlan.fitNeighbourhood names the schedule the page is fitted on (R181), which numbers every build. python/c3d_run.load_config lays this block over connect of the probe settings and refuses a key both files hold.

roadFolder.note: R344, Q073. A front corner takes a road level only from a surface of roadSurfaces that covers it within snapM (R157), and snapM must be a finite distance of 0 m to snapMaxM, the largest snap a run takes, so a wide snap never takes a road sideways. The Roads folder was read in full in Round ADDIN and holds no other road level at a corner no road surface covers, notTaken says why for each other source. A plot with such a corner gets no level and is listed in noRoadLevel of the plan summary with the surfaces tried, these reasons beside it, never a guessed value.

notTaken.roadSurfaceC3D: Makkah Phase 1_Road Surface C3D holds 7 TIN surfaces, all among the 18 LandXML files of the data book, the walk of all its handles in a Civil 3D window found no other, the 11 surfaces of its file header are no object of it
notTaken.alignments: Road Surface C3D holds no alignment and no profile by the same walk, the 154 of its file header are no object of it. overrideKeep.note: R330. What every run of python/majority.py keeps of the earlier override list cell for cell, so the plain command gives the committed list. sources: every entry of these jobs, native measured in Round 17, a run writes them again only when --replace native names them. laterFields: per job the fields a later phase measures, laterPhase, a run writes none of them and keeps the earlier ones. Round ADDIN 3c measured the levels of parsons2024Rev6, El @ Entry, the height, the steps and the Prototype-FFL parameter (R339), so none is left to a later phase and a run writes them. --keep adds to it, --replace takes out of it. An entry Bader marks "byHand": true, or one holding a use (R386), is kept one by one whatever --keep names, the entry of the run on its plot, key and field left out, and a run that would drop one off the join is refused.

overrideRounding.note: R385. The rounding the level overrides of each level profile were measured on, by which a build of that profile rounds its levels of R278 and applies its level overrides: R385, the one rule of Python and C#, for parsons2024Rev6, whose overrides Round ADDIN 4b measured again on it (Q080), and pythonRound, the round() of Python on the binary value, for native2022, whose overrides Round 17 measured and no run measures again unless it names --replace native (Q050). A profile whose keyRules hold level rules builds on R385 only, a profile named here by no rounding is refused, and a majority run, which measures on R385, never writes the overrides of a job whose profile names another.

majority.overrideNote: Bader edits this list by hand and marks each entry he edits with "byHand": true at the end of its line, a rerun of python/majority.py keeps such an entry one by one, the other entries of its field measured again, and refuses a run that would drop it (R330). The tool applies the coded rule and then the overrides of a plot whose source is the job of the level profile of the build, parsons by default, native only when a build of native2022 names it (R330), narrowed to the past models a build names. model is the past model the override came from. A level holds its gap to the rule in metres and no real level, the plot is the official number of the location plan. A miss with no value to write, a rule that gives none, is listed in cannot after the overrides with no value and never applied, a build refuses an override with no value (R272, R280). Written by python/majority.py (R272, R330).

kindDiscipline.note: R337. The discipline of the prototype files a key of that kind links where it is not the one a build links, prototypeNames.discipline: an SE model links the STR file of the code.

decidedByQuestion.note: R337, R272. Plots and fields an open question decides, by its ID: the coded rule gives them, majority.py writes no override of them and lists them, the proof of a build counts them apart.

Q017.why: the build links the VD4 file of the Rev 9 code, the key the DP4 file, the hand of a VD4 file is not the hand of a DP4 file

keyRulesBlock.note: R338. What python/key_rules_block.py takes besides majority.json to write keyRules of levelProfile in the rules profile: keyRulesNote, the note of the block, zonePrefix, which plots.csv puts before a zone past_all.csv spells as a number, zoneFrom, a zone no key of the group holds taken from zones that give one value, else refused, with why, nativeRound17, the Native share of Round 17 beside a decision, and the texts of the site facts, the flat ramps and the walls. The group is majority.check.group, the native share that of the other group of majority.groups, the holds those of majority.
keyRulesBlock.keyRulesNote: Round ADDIN 3a (R331 to R335). The rules the 7 Parsons answer keys follow, measured by python/majority.py on round_addin past_all.csv: the candidate coded, its share over the Parsons plots it covers and per key, strong at majority.strongShare, the share of the Native keys beside it (native, this run, nativeRound17, the table of Round 17 where it had one) and the plots it misses, each an override of source parsons in config/overrides. The values are lengths, angles and names, never a coordinate or a level.

workerPeakMiB.commandsNote: R347, Q083. The peak private memory in MiB of a whole command, held before its first read with the floor siteBuild.minFreeGB and before each later read as the rest of it, the peak less what the worker holds, with the floor. read 4,100 MiB, CHOSEN: the highest whole read of button 2 measured, the three drawings, the six road surfaces and the two Rev 9 workbooks, 4,008 MiB on net48 after the review of PR 53 (net48 3,931 to 4,008 and net8.0 3,576 to 3,584 over three runs each, round_addin logs p4cfix_button2_time.txt, and 3,971 on net8.0 in the read parity, p4cfix_parity_read.txt), rounded up to the next 100 MiB. The runs of Round ADDIN 4c peaked at 3,069 to 3,595 on net48 and 3,578 to 3,891 on net8.0 (p4c_button2_time.txt), and the build before the review peaked at 3,899 on net48 in the same state of the PC (p4cfix_time_compare_floor2.txt), so the peak moves with the state of the PC and not with the fixes. A command named here takes no file peak in place of it, the peak of each large drawing above is still held before its read. The build and the other commands have none until a PR measures them

addin.workerPeakNote: R347. The sizes and the private peaks 2,571, 100 and 77 MiB are those of round_addin logs cadreader_peaks_pr49.txt on copies at 67c1fa0, whose peak paged by the OS was 2,571, 101 and 80. The values here are the highest seen: 2,612 MiB of the Road Layout is the claim-checker rerun of PR 49 and 80 MiB of the footprint the first run of 3b, neither output saved, 100 MiB of the baseplan the saved log
addin.workerTimeLimitNote: R347, R348. read 300 s, measured in Round ADDIN 4c: a whole read of button 2 in the worker, the three drawings, the six road surfaces and the two Rev 9 workbooks, took 20.2 to 21.2 s on net48 and 16.8 to 17.0 s on net8.0 over three runs each (round_addin logs p4c_button2_time.txt), so 300 s is about 14 times the longest, room for a slower PC and the location plan read 4d adds, which measures it again. After the review of PR 53 the same read took 20.9 to 47.0 s on net48 and 21.5 to 32.6 s on net8.0 as the free memory of the PC went from 4.4 to 6.6 GiB, the build before the review as long as the head in the same state (p4cfix_button2_time.txt, p4cfix_time_compare_floor1.txt and _floor2.txt), so 300 s is over 6 times the longest. 600 s for the read until 4c, 28 times the 21.2 s of the Road Layout read alone. 60 s for the level Excel, the other commands 600 s until the PR that builds each measures it (CHOSEN in docs/addin-design.md)
addin.workbookRolesNote: R350.
